transcript:
Meeting header:

Duration: ~52 minutes

Recording: Yes

Summary: AtlasPay is evaluating Redwood for low-latency payment orchestration features. Primary concerns: multi-region routing, graceful degradation during GPU outages, private VPC options for PCI-adjacent workloads, and measurable SLA commitments. They asked about fallback policies (model variant fallbacks and regional failover), observability during incidents, and audit logs for compliance. Redwood AE+SE focused on routing policies, cache strategies, and on-prem/private deployment trade-offs.
---
[00:00] Jordan Kim: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, im on the east coast but i think that's okay — uh Lina and Marcus are with me from SE.
[00:12] Maya Patel: hey, thanks. we have a couple teams on here, im maya head of platform at atlaspay, this is samir sro, elliot cto and priya product.
[00:20] Lina Ortega: great, quick agenda — understand your failure modes, SLOs, and what you need for private/dedicated versus hosted. we'll share examples and next steps.
[00:32] Samir Reddy: cool. to start, quick context: atlaspay runs a payments orchestration service that enriches merchant requests with llm-driven risk signals. so latency is sensitive — 95th p99 matters.
[00:45] Elliot James: yeah, for authorizations we have a ~150ms soft target on path for model calls, anything above 300ms we see increased declines.
[00:56] Jordan Kim: ok that's helpful; we usually classify requests into two buckets: fast-path (short prompt, cached prefixes) and heavy-path (longer context for fraud analysis). for fast-path we recommend dedicated capacity or hosted with reserved instances + prefix caching to hit p95.
[01:20] Priya Shah: quick question — when you say prefix caching, is that in-memory on the server or customer-side?
[01:27] Lina Ortega: good q — Redwood's KV/prefix cache is at the runtime tier, per model instance; it caches tokenized prefixes and kv cache entries. for private deployments you can configure the cache sizes and eviction policy. note: naming sometimes shows up as KV cache or "prefix cache" in our docs.
[01:45] Maya Patel: we operate across US-EAST and EU-WEST, want regional routing with automatic failover if a region hits degraded GPU capacity, but we also have a compliance constraint where certain merchant data must stay in-region.
[02:00] Marcus Liu: you can set routing policies that are both region-preference and region-hard-constraint. soft-pref will try preferred region then fallback; hard-constraint prevents cross-regioning for specific routes. we map that to route policies in the console.
[02:18] Samir Reddy: how does Redwood detect region degradation? is it health-check based or capacity-based?
[02:25] Lina Ortega: it's a combination: we monitor per-pool jitter, queue lengths, and p50/p95 token latency. thresholds can be custom. when a pool breaches policy thresholds we trigger a reroute — with canary steps for A/B or immediate failover depending on your policy.
[02:40] Elliot James: what's the typical time to failover? we need <30s for failover detection and reroute, ideally without client retries.
[02:48] Jordan Kim: with aggressive thresholds we can signal within ~10-20s, but full traffic shifting to a remote region may incur cold-start latencies for KV warmup if the cache wasn't present — you can mitigate with cross-region pre-warms or maintain a small standby cache.
[03:05] Priya Shah: you mentioned model variants — can we fallback to a smaller/faster model automatically when a larger model is overloaded?
[03:13] Lina Ortega: yes — policy-based model variant fallbacks are supported. you define acceptable quality tiers, cost/latency tradeoffs; in runtime we can drop to a quantized or smaller family with automatic sampling to monitor regressions. we tie this to quality monitoring so regressions trigger alerts.
[03:32] Maya Patel: that sounds promising — but for PCI-adjacent workloads we prefer VPC/private deployments. how different are the ops for private vs dedicated?
[03:42] Marcus Liu: in Private you run the control plane on your VPC or an air-gapped environment; we provide the same APIs but the traffic, keys, and audit logs stay in your network. Dedicated is Redwood-managed reserved capacity in our cloud, with tenancy isolation but still through our control plane. ops complexity rises with Private — you own infra, patching, but gain control for compliance.
[04:03] Samir Reddy: do you support HSM/KMS integrations? we use AWS KMS + external HSM for some keys.
[04:10] Lina Ortega: yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM. for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer keys via KMS integration; for Private we can integrate with your on-prem HSMs.
[04:22] Elliot James: audit logs and immutability? that's non-negotiable for us.
[04:26] Jordan Kim: we provide audit logs for inference requests, configuration changes, rollout events. in Private you can push logs to your SIEM; in Hosted we provide log exports and long retention add-ons.
[04:36] Priya Shah: what's the SLA for hosted vs dedicated?
[04:40] Marcus Liu: Hosted has a baseline SLA focused on uptime for control plane and best-effort inference. Dedicated customers get contractual SLOs for latency and throughput with credits for missed targets. Private is negotiated — since infra is customer-managed, uptime SLA focuses on control plane connectivity and support commitments.
[05:00] Maya Patel: can you share examples of latency SLOs? p95 p50 targets?
[05:05] Lina Ortega: for dedicated we have customers on p95 <150ms for short-sequence models. for longer sequences p95 increases; we publish model performance profiles, but exact guarantees are in the dedicated contract.
[05:18] Samir Reddy: what about graceful degradation strategies — e.g., degrade to cached response or respond with a partial result?
[05:25] Lina Ortega: you can define policy chains: 1) try primary model, 2) if overload/timeout -> fallback small model, 3) if that fails -> cached prefix response, 4) if still failing -> pre-defined static safe-message. we also support hedging (parallel requests to multiple pools) for very latency-sensitive calls but that costs more.
[05:46] Elliot James: hedging sounds expensive, curious about cost calculus.
[05:49] Jordan Kim: yes it's tradeoff; Redwood Optimize can run a cost-sensitivity analysis across workloads to recommend hedging only for the narrowest set that truly needs it.
[05:59] Priya Shah: in incident scenarios, how do you surface per-token costs and root cause?
[06:05] Marcus Liu: our console provides token-level breakdowns, model traces, and per-request latency waterfall. during incidents we open a triage channel and can provide trace dumps. for Private deployments you can configure extended telemetry.
[06:20] Maya Patel: ok next: network partitions — say us-east loses connectivity to our EU region but instances are healthy, do you automatically route to a third region?
[06:29] Lina Ortega: yes if policy allows it. you can set multi-tier fallback: preferred -> fallback region -> global pool. you can also block cross-region for specific tenant IDs to satisfy data residency.
[06:42] Samir Reddy: how do you handle KV cache warmup when failing over? i.e., do we get huge latency spikes until warmed?
[06:48] Marcus Liu: unless you pre-warm, first requests will miss cache and you'll see increased latency. strategies: 1) maintain small warm standby in fallback region; 2) snapshot/replicate hot prefixes asynchronously; 3) use conservative failover thresholds that trigger before cache eviction. each has cost vs complexity tradeoffs.
[07:10] Elliot James: for a pilot we want to test model fallback + region failover. what's a minimal viable pilot look like?
[07:16] Jordan Kim: typical pilot: 1) pick 2 critical routes (fast-path + heavy-path), 2) run hosted with reserved dedicated pool for fast-path, 3) enable model-variant fallback policy and soft-pref region routing, 4) run canary traffic up to 5% to validate responses and monitor regressions for 2 weeks.
[07:33] Priya Shah: timeline to pilot? we have Q1 exec ok for production.
[07:36] Jordan Kim: we can start pilot in 2-3 weeks: security questionnaire, connect SSO, sign pilot contract, spin up dedicated pool. for Private it's longer (~6-8 weeks) with infra setup.
[07:49] Samir Reddy: we need to run local benchmarks against our 150ms p95 target. can you provide a perf harness for the pilot?
[07:55] Lina Ortega: yes we'll share a benchmark harness and a test spreadsheet. we'll also share a sample traffic generator and model profiles.
[08:03] Maya Patel: compatibility Q: we run internal inference logic that relies on kv cache eviction tuning, will we be able to tune eviction/gc on private?
[08:11] Marcus Liu: yes, Private exposes config for cache sizes, TTLs, and eviction policy; Dedicated has configurable knobs but some are managed by Redwood to maintain cluster stability.
[08:23] Priya Shah: any security reviews customers commonly ask for?
[08:26] Jordan Kim: SOC 2 report, pen test summary, network diagrams, and for Private, architecture diagrams and KMS/HSM integration docs. we'll send the security pack after the call.
[08:36] Elliot James: do you do data residency proofs/audits?
[08:40] Lina Ortega: we can provide audit logs and attestations for hosted and dedicated customers; for Private you own the logs but we help with the schema for audits.
[08:49] Maya Patel: ok last — pricing expectation for dedicated capacity? rough numbers to present to finance.
[08:56] Jordan Kim: rough ballpark: small dedicated pool for light production is in the low thousands per month; larger enterprise pools that hit <150ms p95 at scale are higher. exact pricing depends on model family, throughput, and retention. we'll follow up with a tailored quote.
[09:12] Samir Reddy: competitor check — we have PoCs with CumulusAI and Selfhostr. how do you compare?
[09:18] Marcus Liu: high-level: Redwood focuses on production economics and unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private. competitors often excel at either pure self-host or managed endpoints. we'll share a short comparison doc.
[09:30] Priya Shah: perfect.
[09:32] Jordan Kim: quick recap:
 - Pilot in 2-3 weeks for hosted/dedicated hybrid
 - Redwood will send security pack, perf harness, pilot quote, and routing/policy sample configs
 - AtlasPay to confirm pilot routes and timeline by next Wed
[09:50] Maya Patel: noted. action items below.
